summary: PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16 is a careful, source-faithful extraction, and its theorems hold up. I re-read the Annals text in full against arXiv v2 (both hashes match the review's), and I found new mathematical errors and a large duplication. The work breaks in 13 findings: 3 high, 5 medium and 5 low. High: (1) Corollary 1.9 of v2 (1.4 in print) has both exponents wrong: the Poincaré dual is q^{1+(g−1)r²}A(z^{−1}), not q^{2(1+(g−1)r²)}A(z^{−1}), and the components are counted by H^{2(1+(g−1)r²)}, not H^{1+(g−1)r²}. This is checked at r = 1, at (g,r) = (1,2) and by Poincaré duality. E4's 'unmatched parenthesis' correction, confirmed by the review, makes the formula false, and item 12 copies both errors. (2) Item 11 copies v2's Poincaré-polynomial identity without the sign (−1)^n, which is false already at r = 1. Print corrects it, and this, with v2's dimension slip, is an unrecorded mistake corrected in print. (3) Route 1 duplicates PAPER-YU-23's routes, accepted earlier the same day. Yu sends Schiffmann's Theorem 1.2, the counting polynomial, purity and the Poincaré polynomial, Krull–Schmidt, the Higgs moduli, the density of Weil tuples, the plethystic Log and the GSp character ring to its GS counting Part II, to QM.0 and to ClassicalGroupsPartII. Both design jobs are pending. Medium: the independence of d and the integrality are recorded as open, but Mellit proved them (Theorem 1.1, arXiv:1707.04214). Items 54 and 55 claim Q[T_g]^{W_g}, where the paper proves only K_g (v2 Corollary 8.1 is corrected in print; Theorem 7.1 has a gap, which for N = 0 is the paper's own conjecture). Item 9's 'planned at ET.2b' does not hold: ET.2b does not cover the canonical twist, stability or the moduli space, and the route and the review contradict each other on who owns them. Krull–Schmidt and Fitting are already in Tau Ceti. The Section 5 derivation, (5.14)–(5.22), and four proof facts have no item. Low: uncited declarations and QM.0's q-binomial node; two print-only cross-reference slips in Lemma 6.1; missing prerequisites; over-stated planned statuses for items 14 and 43; stale 'could not be consulted' text. Not repeated: RT-AREA-etale/1 and FIX-RT-AREA-etale already cover route 3 (the density item 36), the [Del74, 3.5.3] reference, the v2 twist and M_g slips, and the missing sourceVersions.

No finding asks for a change to this session's files.

findings.where: PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16/12 (Corollary 1.9 of arXiv v2 = Corollary 1.4 of the Annals text) and sourceIssue PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16/E4 (its third part, and its review verdict)
findings.claim: Both exponents in the paper's corollary on the stable global nilpotent cone are wrong, and item 12 copies both. The source issue records only a missing parenthesis, and its fix makes the formula false. (i) The Poincaré dual has to be Ā_{g,r,d}(z) = q^{1+(g−1)r²}·A_{g,r,d}(z^{−1}), not q^{2(1+(g−1)r²)}·A_{g,r,d}(z^{−1}). E4 reads the printed 'q^{2(1+(g−1)r^2}' as a dropped closing parenthesis and corrects it to q^{2(1+(g−1)r²)}. The review confirmed that reading, and the register now carries it as the correction. With that exponent, |Λ^st_{r,d}(F_q)| comes out q^{1+(g−1)r²} times too large. (ii) The degree in (ii) has to be the top degree 2(1+(g−1)r²), not 1+(g−1)r²: the number of irreducible components equals the dimension of H^{2(1+(g−1)r²)}, not of H^{1+(g−1)r²}. It looks as though '2(' moved from (ii) into (i). The mistake affects a stated result, so it is an error, not a misprint, and the E4 correction has to change.
findings.evidence: Paper: arXiv v2 p. 5, Corollary 1.9: 'Moreover, |Λst_r,d(Fq)| = Ā_g,r,d(σX) where Ā_g,r,d(z1,…,z2g) = q^{2(1+(g−1)r^2} Ag,r,d(z1^{−1},…,z2g^{−1}) is the Poincarré dual of Ag,r,d. ii) (k = Fq, C). We have dim H^{1+(g−1)r²}(Λst_r,d, C) = dim H^{1+(g−1)r²}(Higgsst_r,d, C) = Ag,r,d(0). In particular, the number of irreducible components of Λst_r,d is equal to Ag,r,d(0).' The Annals version, Corollary 1.4, p. 301, is the same (checked on a rendered page image at 300 dpi): 'q^{2(1+(g−1)r²} A_{g,r,d}(z1^{−1},…)' and 'dim H^{1+(g−1)r²}(Λst_{r,d}, C) = dim H^{1+(g−1)r²}(Higgsst_{r,d}, C) = A_{g,r,d}(0)'. Check r = 1, any g ≥ 1. Higgs^st_{1,d} = T*Pic^d = Pic^d × H⁰(Ω), the Hitchin map is the projection to H⁰(Ω), and Λ^st_{1,d} = Pic^d. So |Λ(F_q)| = |Jac(F_q)| = ∏_{i=1}^{2g}(1−σ_i). By Theorem 1.6's example, A_{g,1,d} = ∏(1−α_i), so A(σ^{−1}) = ∏(σ_i−1)/∏σ_i = |Jac(F_q)|/q^g. Then q^{1+(g−1)}·A(σ^{−1}) = |Jac(F_q)|, which is correct, while q^{2g}·A(σ^{−1}) = q^g|Jac(F_q)|, which is wrong. For (ii): Λ = Pic^d has one component, and A(0) = 1 = dim H^{2g}(Jac), whereas dim H^g(Jac) = C(2g,g), which is 2 already for g = 1. Check g = 1, r = 2, d = 1. By Atiyah, A_{1,2,1} = (1−α_1)(1−α_2), and Λ^st_{2,1} ≅ E. Then q·A(σ^{−1}) = (σ_1−1)(σ_2−1) = |E(F_q)|, and dim H²(E) = 1 = A_{1,2,1}(0) = C(1,1), while dim H¹(E) = 2. General argument: put D = 1+(g−1)r². Then Higgs^st has dimension 2D and retracts onto the proper variety Λ. By Theorem 1.2, Σ_n (−1)^n tr(Fr | H^n_c(Higgs)) = q^D·A(σ). Poincaré duality, H^i(Λ) = H^i(Higgs) ≅ H^{4D−i}_c(Higgs)^∨(−2D), turns each eigenvalue λ into q^{2D}/λ. Since q(σ^{−1}) = q^{−1}, this gives |Λ(F_q)| = q^{2D}·(q^D A)(σ^{−1}) = q^D·A(σ^{−1}). By published Corollary 1.3, the coefficient of t^{2D} in Σ(−1)^n dim H^n_c t^n = t^{2D}A(t,…,t) is A(0) = dim H^{2D}_c = dim H^{2D}(Higgs) = dim H^{2D}(Λ).
findings.fix: (1) Item 12: in (i), replace 'Ā_{g,r,d}(z) = q^{2(1+(g−1)r²)}A_{g,r,d}(z^{−1})' by 'Ā_{g,r,d}(z) = q^{1+(g−1)r²}A_{g,r,d}(z^{−1})'; in (ii), replace 'dim H^{1+(g−1)r²}(Λ^st_{r,d}, C) = dim H^{1+(g−1)r²}(Higgs^st_{r,d}, C) = A_{g,r,d}(0)' by 'dim H^{2(1+(g−1)r²)}(Λ^st_{r,d}, C) = dim H^{2(1+(g−1)r²)}(Higgs^st_{r,d}, C) = A_{g,r,d}(0)'. Add the r = 1 and (g,r,d) = (1,2,1) checks to the item's note as acceptance tests. (2) E4: delete the sentence on the unmatched parenthesis, together with its published-version clause, and keep E4 as the two index misprints. (3) Add a new sourceIssue, PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16/E8 (after the E5–E7 proposed by FIX-RT-AREA-etale). Kind 'error', affects 'a stated result', known 'new'. Locator: 'Corollary 1.9 i) and ii), arXiv v2 p. 5; Corollary 1.4 (i) and (ii), Annals p. 301'. Printed: the two displays quoted above. Correction: 'Ā_{g,r,d}(z) = q^{1+(g−1)r²}A_{g,r,d}(z^{−1}); dim H^{2(1+(g−1)r²)}(Λ^st) = dim H^{2(1+(g−1)r²)}(Higgs^st) = A_{g,r,d}(0)'. Reason: the r = 1 and (1,2,1) computations and the duality argument above. Searched: the arXiv versions, the Annals text and page, and a search for an erratum. (4) The file then needs sourceVersions (PROTOCOL section 18). Add the arXiv v2 and Annals entries that FIX-RT-AREA-etale 1.7 proposes.

findings.where: PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16/11 (Corollaries 1.6–1.8 of arXiv v2 = Corollaries 1.3 and 1.5 of the Annals text); sourceIssues (none recorded)
findings.claim: Item 11 states 'Σ_n dim H_c^n(Higgs^st_{r,d}(X̄), Q̄_l) t^n = t^{2(1+(g−1)r²)} A_{g,r,d}(t,…,t)', and says the same holds over C. This is false. The sign (−1)^n is missing (equivalently, A should be evaluated at (−t,…,−t)). The item copies arXiv v2 Corollaries 1.6 and 1.7, which the Annals version corrects to Σ_n (−1)^n dim H_c^n t^n. The extraction records no source issue for this preprint slip, although section 18 records mistakes already corrected in print. It also misses a second slip corrected in print: v2 derives Corollary 1.8 (degree 2(1+(g−1)r²)) 'from the fact that the moduli space Higgs^st_{r,d}(X_C) is connected and of dimension 1+(g−1)r²'. The dimension is 2(1+(g−1)r²).
findings.evidence: arXiv v2 p. 4, Corollary 1.6: 'Σ_n dim H^n_c(Higgs^st_{r,d}(X), Ql) t^n = t^{2(1+(g−1)r²)} A_{g,r,d}(t,t,…,t)'. Corollary 1.7 is the same over C. v2 p. 4, before Corollary 1.8: 'From the fact that the moduli space Higgsst_r,d(XC) is connected and of dimension 1+(g−1)r², we immediately deduce'. Annals p. 300, Corollary 1.3 (i) and (ii): 'Σ_n (−1)^n dim H^n_c(Higgsst_{r,d}(X̄), Q̄l) t^n = t^{2(1+(g−1)r²)} A_{g,r,d}(t,t,…,t)' (rendered page image). Annals p. 352, proof of Corollary 1.5: 'connected and of dimension 2(1 + (g − 1)r²)'. Check r = 1: Higgs^st_{1,d} = Pic^d × A^g, so H^n_c = H^{n−2g}(Jac) and Σ_n dim H^n_c t^n = t^{2g}(1+t)^{2g}. But A_{g,1,d}(t,…,t) = (1−t)^{2g}, so v2's identity fails for every g ≥ 1, and the signed identity holds. The same happens for g = 1, r = 2, d = 1 (Higgs^st = T*E, A = (1−α_1)(1−α_2)). The paper's own proof gives the sign. The multiplicity of σ^I is a_I, where A = Σ a_I(−z)^I, and H^n_c has weight n, so Σ dim H^n_c t^n = t^{2D}A(−t,…,−t).
findings.fix: Item 11: replace 'Σ_n dim H_c^n(Higgs^st_{r,d}(X̄), Q̄_l) t^n = t^{2(1+(g−1)r²)} A_{g,r,d}(t,…,t)' by 'Σ_n (−1)^n dim H_c^n(Higgs^st_{r,d}(X̄), Q̄_l) t^n = t^{2(1+(g−1)r²)} A_{g,r,d}(t,…,t)', and make the same change for X_C. Add the published locators (Corollaries 1.3 and 1.5, pp. 300–302). Add two sourceIssues. First, kind 'misprint', known 'corrected in the published version: Annals 183 (2016), Corollary 1.3, p. 300, which has the sign (−1)^n', locator 'Corollaries 1.6 and 1.7, arXiv v2 p. 4'. Second, kind 'misprint', known 'corrected in the published version, proof of Corollary 1.5, p. 352', locator 'sentence before Corollary 1.8, arXiv v2 p. 4', correction 'of dimension 2(1+(g−1)r²)'.

findings.where: PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16/8 (Conjectures 1.3/1.4 of v2 = 1.7/1.8 in print), note of /3, route 1 brief part (8), prerequisites
findings.claim: Item 8 records the independence of A_{g,r,d} from d as open. Its note says 'It is a conjecture, not a theorem, and must be recorded as such', and route 1's brief says 'the conjecture that A_{g,r,d} is independent of d (proved for r prime) … recorded as conjectures and not as theorems … recorded as open'. The note of /3 likewise leaves 'Conjecturally A_{g,r,d} lies in Q[T_g]^{W_g}' open. Mellit proved both for g ≥ 1 in 2017, building on this paper. For every d, A_{g,r,d} = H_{g,r}(q, 1, α_1, …, α_g), a Laurent polynomial that is independent of d. Laurent polynomials in q and the α_i are regular functions on the torus T_g, so A_{g,r,d} ∈ Q[T_g]^{W_g} and no localisation is needed. The coprime-d case also follows from GWZ-20's item 70, already extracted: #M^d_{GL_n}(X)(k) = #M^e_{GL_n}(X)(k), which with Theorem 1.2 gives independence of d. Following the brief, a design job would plan these as open conjectures and duplicate nothing, but it would state a theorem as an open conjecture and miss its source. Mellit is not among the prerequisites.
findings.evidence: A. Mellit, 'Poincaré polynomials of moduli spaces of Higgs bundles and character varieties (no punctures)', arXiv:1707.04214v1 (13 July 2017), read 30 September 2026 (SHA-256 300492e260092efd696f2e2d046603ab36ae0981c0f504709762b7e3cf6f9f6a); published in Invent. Math. 221 (2020). Theorem 1.1, p. 2: 'Let g ≥ 1 … Hg = −(1 − q)(1 − z) Log Ωg … Then for all r ≥ 1 Hg,r is a Laurent polynomial in q, z and α1, …, αg, and for all d Ag,r,d is obtained by setting z = 1 in Hg,r: Ag,r,d(q, α1, …, αg) = Hg,r(q, 1, α1, …, αg).' Also on p. 2: 'Theorem 1.1 is a direct corollary of Theorem 5.2 and [Sch14]', where [Sch14] is this paper. The abstract says the result 'implies … the conjecture of Hausel and Thaddeus on independence of E-polynomials on the degree'. PAPER-YU-23/046 cites the same theorem ('[Me17, Thm 1.1] with Schiffmann [Sc16] … For every … e ∈ Z'). PAPER-GROECHENIG-WYSS-ZIEGLER-20/70: 'Independence of the degree for GL_n Higgs point counts … (the coprime, independence-of-d part of Mozgovoy–Schiffmann's conjecture)'. Schiffmann, Annals p. 300: 'Conjecturally, A_{g,r,d} belongs to Q[T_g]^{W_g} and there is no need to consider the localization K_g'.
findings.fix: Item 8. Keep the paper's statement and its locator. Replace the note's last sentence with: 'Stated as a conjecture in the paper and proved there for r prime (Appendix C). It is now a theorem: Mellit, Invent. Math. 221 (2020), arXiv:1707.04214, Theorem 1.1, shows for g ≥ 1 and every d that A_{g,r,d} = H_{g,r}(q,1,α), a Laurent polynomial independent of d. For coprime d it also follows from GWZ-20 item 70 with Theorem 1.2.' Item 3: add to the note that Mellit's theorem gives A_{g,r,d} ∈ Q[T_g]^{W_g}. Route 1 brief (8): move 'the conjecture that A_{g,r,d} is independent of d (proved for r prime)' out of the list of open conjectures, as 'Mellit's theorem (degree independence and integrality), imported or planned with Mellit's paper as source'. Add Mellit's paper to prerequisites.

findings.claim: Two items give counting polynomials in Q[T_g]^{W_g}, which the paper does not prove. (a) Item 55 copies v2's Corollary 8.1: 'polynomials A^{≥ν}_{g,r,d}, A^{≤ν}_{g,r,d} ∈ Q[T_g]^{W_g}'. The Annals version corrects this to K_g, the only ring that the proof of Theorem 1.1 ('The proof of Theorem 1.1 yields the following') gives. (b) Item 54 copies Theorem 7.1, which in both versions asserts 'a unique polynomial A_{g,p,α} ∈ Q[T_g]^{W_g}', for any N ≥ 0. For N = 0 there are no parabolic points, and Theorem 7.1 is Theorem 1.1 with the localisation removed. The paper itself calls that a conjecture (p. 300). The only proof offered is 'completely parallel to that of Theorem 1.1', which gives elements of K_g. As printed, Theorem 7.1 asserts more than the paper proves (a gap). For N = 0, Mellit's theorem (finding 4) now closes it; for N ≥ 1 nothing in the paper does. Neither point is a recorded source issue.
findings.evidence: arXiv v2 p. 33, Corollary 8.1: 'there exists polynomials A≥ν g,r,d, A≤ν g,r,d ∈ Q[Tg]Wg'. Annals p. 353, Corollary 8.1: 'there exist polynomials A≥ν g,r,d, A≤ν g,r,d ∈ Kg'. Theorem 7.1 (v2 p. 32; Annals pp. 352–353): 'For any g ≥ 0, any positive integer N ≥ 0 … there exists a unique polynomial Ag,p,α ∈ Q[Tg]Wg'. §7.2: 'The proof of Theorem 7.1 is completely parallel to that of Theorem 1.1'. Theorem 1.1 (Annals p. 299) gives 'a unique element Ag,r,d ∈ Kg', and p. 300 says 'Conjecturally, Ag,r,d belongs to Q[Tg]Wg and there is no need to consider the localization Kg'. Items 54 and 55 read '∈ Q[T_g]^{W_g}'.
findings.fix: Item 55: replace 'A^{≥ν}_{g,r,d}, A^{≤ν}_{g,r,d} ∈ Q[T_g]^{W_g}' by '∈ K_g', and add the published locator (Annals p. 353). Item 54: write the conclusion as 'A_{g,p,α} ∈ K_g (the paper asserts Q[T_g]^{W_g}, but its proof, parallel to Theorem 1.1, gives K_g; for N = 0 integrality is Mellit's theorem)'. Add two sourceIssues. First, a misprint: v2 Corollary 8.1, 'Q[T_g]^{W_g}' for 'K_g', known 'corrected in the published version, Corollary 8.1, p. 353'. Second, a gap: Theorem 7.1, 'Q[T_g]^{W_g}' is claimed but only K_g follows from the parallel proof, and for N = 0 this contradicts the conjectural status stated on p. 300. Affects 'a stated result', known 'new; for N = 0 settled by Mellit (Invent. Math. 221 (2020), Theorem 1.1)'.

findings.where: PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16/9 (status 'planned' at ET.2b and GS.0), /12, route 1 brief part (7), route 4 and its review reason
findings.claim: Item 9 is marked planned at EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.2b, but ET.2b does not plan what the item states. The item needs Higgs fields for the canonical twist Ω_X, slope (semi)stability of Higgs sheaves, and, for coprime (r,d), the moduli space Higgs^st_{r,d} as a smooth connected scheme with its G_m-gerbe Higgs^st_{r,d}(X). ET.2b plans Higgs fields 'twisted by a chosen sufficiently positive divisor'; deg Ω_X = 2g−2 is excluded, and the stage has no stability condition and no coarse moduli space. Corollary 1.4's proof (item 12) also needs the properness of the Hitchin map on Higgs^st ('Since µ is proper') and the stable global nilpotent cone, which ET.2b does not plan for GL_r with the canonical twist. The files contradict each other on who plans these. Route 1's brief (7) tells the new roadmap to plan 'Higgs sheaves and bundles with the canonical twist, their stability, the moduli stack and the smooth moduli space for coprime (r,d), the Hitchin map and the stable global nilpotent cone'. The review of route 4 says they 'belong there [ET.2b] and are imported rather than re-planned by route 1'. Yu 036 (stable Higgs coarse moduli) is 'missing' and in Yu's GS counting Part II; GWZ-20 routes the SL_n analogue (item 62) to TopologicalMirrorSymmetryForHitchinSystems. So there are three candidate owners and no decision.

Prove algebraicity, finite-type bounds, the required proper anisotropic quotient, and exact component-group actions.' It says nothing about stability or moduli spaces. Schiffmann, Annals §6.2, pp. 336–337: 'A Higgs sheaf … θ ∈ Hom(V, V ⊗ ΩX) … semistable (resp. stable) if … µ(W) ≤ µ(V) … The stack Higgsst r,d(X) is a Gm-gerbe over a smooth connected scheme over k'. findings.where: PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16/15 (Krull–Schmidt), /16 (radical of End), note and route 1 brief ('Krull–Schmidt for finite-length modules … from the Tau Ceti roadmap on quiver representations')
findings.claim: The note of item 15 treats Krull–Schmidt as planned in a roadmap ('The Tau Ceti roadmap on quiver representations builds Fitting's lemma, the local-endomorphism-ring criterion and the Krull–Schmidt theorem … and records that Mathlib has neither'), and concludes that the needed statement, 'Krull–Schmidt for a Hom-finite category with local endomorphism rings of indecomposables', is not covered. At the pinned Tau Ceti commit these are built, and in Azumaya's generality with no finiteness hypothesis on the module: a direct sum of modules with local endomorphism rings has its summands matched with any indecomposable decomposition. Fitting's lemma in the form 'indecomposable of finite length ⇒ local endomorphism ring' is also built, as is existence of decompositions. For Coh(X), only the transfer is missing: End(M) is a finite-dimensional k-algebra, so Fitting gives a local End, and Azumaya's theorem applies inside the category. Item 16's radical computation rests on Mathlib's nilpotent Jacobson radical and semisimple quotient of an Artinian ring. Neither item cites any of this.

findings.where: PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16 items 37–42 and 7 (Section 5), items 19 and 2 (Section 2), items 10 and 52 (Section 6)
findings.claim: The derivation of Theorem 1.6 and several facts used in the proofs have no item, although the extraction's policy is that every key step is an item. Missing from Section 5: (a) the residue formula (5.14)–(5.15), which computes Y^{≥0}_{r_t,…,r_1} for arbitrary ranks from the rank-one shuffle formula through Theorem 4.2(iv); (b) the Jordan-type sum Ξ_r(z) and its evaluation (5.16)–(5.18), Ξ_r = q^{(g−1)⟨λ,λ⟩}·∏_{s∈λ}ζ*_X(q^{−1−l(s)}z^{a(s)})·H_r(z)·Exp(|X(F_q)|z/((q−1)(1−z)))·T^r, including the bijection between generic Jordan types and partitions (§5.6); (c) the generating identity (5.21), Exp(Σ_{r>0,d} A^{≥0}_{g,r,d} z^d T^r/(q−1)) = Σ_λ q^{(g−1)⟨λ,λ⟩}J_λ(z)H_λ(z)T^{|λ|} in K_g[[T,z]], which is the heart of the proof; (d) the torsion count A^{≥0}_{0,d}(X⊗F_{q^l}) = |X(F_{q^l})|, used to pass from (5.19) to (5.20); (e) the periodicity step (5.22), A^{≥0}_{g,r}(z) = P_{g,r}(z) + Σ_{d<r} A_{g,r,d}z^d/(1−z^r), from which the residue formula follows. Missing from Sections 1, 2 and 6: (f) A_{r,d}(X) depends only on d mod r (tensoring by a degree-one line bundle); (g) the Galois-descent step of Proposition 2.2 (Lemma 2.6 in print), including triviality of H¹(Gal, Aut M) for the connected group Aut(M) by Steinberg and Grothendieck, and the identities (2.4)–(2.5); (h) for coprime (r,d), every indecomposable bundle is geometrically indecomposable with End(F)/rad = k, used in Lemma 6.2 (published) and in the count of Y_1(k). (i) The closed formula for A_{g,2,d} in the examples after Theorem 1.6 is not recorded, although it is the natural acceptance test. I checked it: at g = 0 it gives 0, and at g = 1 it gives (1−α_1)(1−α_2) = |E(F_q)|, as Atiyah's classification requires.
findings.evidence: Annals §5.5 p. 331, (5.14)–(5.15): 'by Theorem 4.2(iv), we have Y^{≥0}_r(q^{½(1−r_t)}z^{(t)}_1, …) = q^{a(r)} vol_1^{−n} ∏ vol_{r_i} · Res_r[…]'. §5.6 pp. 331–333, (5.16)–(5.18) and Lemma 5.5. §5.7 p. 334, (5.21): 'we have the following equality in Kg[[T, z]]: Exp(Σ_{r>0,d} A≥0_{g,r,d} z^d T^r/(q−1)) = Σ_λ {q^{(g−1)⟨λ,λ⟩} Jλ(z)Hλ(z)T^{|λ|}}', and 'Observe that A≥0_{0,d}(X ⊗Fq Fql) = |X(Fql)| since a geometrically indecomposable torsion sheaf … is the indecomposable d-fold self extension of the structure sheaf of a rational point'. §5.8 pp. 334–335, (5.22). §1.2 p. 299: 'Ar,d(X) only depends on the residue of d modulo r'. Lemma 2.6 p. 310: 'By Steinberg's and Grothendieck's theorems … the Galois cohomology groups H^i(G, Aut(M)) are trivial (resp. neutral)'. Lemma 6.2 p. 341: 'F is indecomposable (and thus also geometrically indecomposable as (r, d) are coprime). By Fitting's lemma, End(F) is a local k-algebra with End(F)/rad(End(F)) = k'. p. 349: 'Ir,d … indecomposable (and hence geometrically indecomposable)'. The r = 2 formula (p. 305), evaluated with exact rational arithmetic at g = 0 (value 0) and at g = 1 with α_1α_2 = q (value (1−α_1)(1−α_2)) for q = 3, 7, 11/2 and α_1 = 5/3. None of (a)–(i) is among the 59 items: item 7 states the final formula, and items 37–42 state the ingredients without these identities.
findings.fix: Add to route 1 the following items, with the locators above (v2 locators: §§5.5–5.8, pp. 23–29, Lemma 2.6's proof inside Proposition 2.1, Lemma 6.4): 'Residue formula for Y^{≥0} in arbitrary ranks' ((5.14)–(5.15)); 'The Jordan-type sum Ξ_r(z)' ((5.16)–(5.18), with the bijection between generic Jordan types and partitions); 'The generating identity for A^{≥0}_{g,r,d}' ((5.21), with the torsion count of (d)); 'Periodicity and residue extraction' ((5.22)); 'Dependence on d mod r'; 'Galois descent of indecomposables' (Lemma 2.6, with its H¹ vanishing input and an owner or a request for Lang's theorem); and 'Coprime indecomposables are absolutely indecomposable with residue field k'. findings.where: PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16 sourceIssues (published version, §6.4 p. 340 and proof of Proposition 6.6 p. 347)
findings.claim: The published text relabels Lemma 6.1, but two references to it keep the old letters, so they now point to the wrong parts. In v2 the parts are a) semistable Higgs bundles, b) indecomposable bundles, c) kernels, d) destabilising subsheaves. In print they are (a) semistable Higgs bundles, (b) indecomposable bundles, (c) destabilising subsheaves, (d) kernels, (e) L_1 strongly generated by L_2. On p. 340, 'by Lemma 6.1(b) the stack [µ⁻¹(0)/G] contains Higgs^st_{r,d}(X)' needs (a); v2 says 'by condition a)'. On p. 347, 'by the defining property (d) of (L1, L2) there exists a destabilizing subsheaf' needs (c); v2's d) was correct. Both slips are in print only, and neither is recorded.
findings.evidence: Annals p. 338, Lemma 6.1: '(a) any semistable Higgs bundle (V, θ) of class α is strongly generated by L1; (b) any indecomposable vector bundle V of class α is strongly generated by L1; (c) for any unstable Higgs sheaf (F, θ) of class α there exists a destabilizing Higgs subsheaf G ⊂ F which is strongly generated by L1; (d) for any coherent sheaf V of class α and any epimorphism φ : L1 ⊗ V ↠ V, Ker(φ) is strongly generated by L2'. p. 340: 'In particular, by Lemma 6.1(b) the stack [µ−1(0)/G] contains Higgsst r,d(X) as an open substack.' p. 347: 'Then by the defining property (d) of (L1, L2) there exists a destabilizing subsheaf W ∈ S′X'. arXiv v2 p. 26: 'In particular, by condition a) the stack [µ−1(0)/G] contains Higgsstr,d(X)'; v2 p. 30: 'by the defining property d) of (L1, L2) there exists a destabi[lizing]'.
findings.fix: Add one sourceIssue, kind 'misprint', affects 'nothing', known 'new'. Locator: 'published version only: §6.4, p. 340, and proof of Proposition 6.6, p. 347; arXiv v2 is correct (pp. 26, 30)'. Printed: the two sentences above. findings.claim: Several papers that the proofs rely on, and that the atlas does not cover, are missing from prerequisites (papers.json has none of them). Mozgovoy–Schiffmann, 'Counting Higgs bundles' [MS14], is the companion paper: it proves Theorem 1.2 in all characteristics and gives the detailed proof of Proposition 3.1 ('We refer to [MS14, Prop. 5.1]'). García-Prada–Heinloth–Schmitt [GPHS14] is the model for Proposition 3.1 ('completely analogous to [GPHS14, Prop. 3.1, Cor. 3.2]') and, with [GPH13], the source of the existence of the counting polynomial, of purity and of the moduli of chains Z. Harder–Narasimhan [HN75, Prop. 2.3.4] is the source of Siegel's formula (Theorem 4.1(i)). Heinloth [Hei12] computes the cohomology of Coh_γ, an alternative route to Theorem 4.1(ii)–(iii). Mellit is covered by finding 4, and Katz–Sarnak by FIX-RT-AREA-etale.
findings.evidence: Annals p. 300: 'In the companion paper [MS14] written in collaboration with S. Mozgovoy, we give a different proof of the above theorem … which works in all characteristics'. p. 314: 'The proofs of statements (i)–(iii) are completely analogous to [GPHS14, Prop. 3.1, Cor. 3.2] … We refer to [MS14, Prop. 5.1], where a more detailed argument is given'. p. 317: 'The first statement is known as the Siegel formula; see [HN75, Prop. 2.3.4]'. p. 317: 'the cohomology … of the moduli stacks Cohγ have been determined for all γ by J. Heinloth (see [Hei12, Th. 1])'. p. 348: 'An explicit description of Z is given and studied in [GPHS14] (the so-called moduli of chains on X)'. papers.json contains none of 'Mozgovoy', 'Heinloth', 'Narasimhan' or 'Mellit' (grep count 0).

Schmitt, On the motives of moduli of chains and Higgs bundles, J. Eur. Math. Soc. 16 (2014), 2617–2668, doi:10.4171/JEMS/494; O. García-Prada and J. Heinloth, The y-genus of the moduli space of PGL_n-Higgs bundles on a curve (for degree coprime to n), Duke Math. J. 162 (2013), 2731–2749, doi:10.1215/00127094-2381369; G. Harder and M. S. Narasimhan, On the cohomology groups of moduli spaces of vector bundles on curves, Math. Ann. 212 (1974/75), 215–248, doi:10.1007/BF01357141; A. Mellit (finding 4). For each, give the use quoted above as the 'why'.

findings.where: PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16/14 (planned at GS.0) and /43 (planned at R09.2)
findings.claim: Two planned statuses claim more than the cited stages plan. Item 14 needs the Euler form ⟨F,G⟩ on K_0(Coh X) and its formula ⟨(r,d),(r′,d′)⟩ = (1−g)rr′ + (rd′ − r′d). It also needs Harder–Narasimhan filtrations of coherent sheaves (torsion included), their invariance under field extension, the categories C_{≥ν} and C_{≤ν} with closure of C_{≥0} under quotients and extensions, and the finiteness of D(α). GS.0 plans only the Harder–Narasimhan bounded opens of Bun_G. Its packet's GS.0 nodes (partial, 24 September, after this route was accepted) include none of the above, and its remaining list says 'Harder-Narasimhan filtrations and slopes of G-bundles … the entire theory has to be built'. Item 43's note says R09.2 includes 'the tangent-space description and the strong-generation condition'; R09.2's text mentions neither.

findings.claim: When the review added the published locations, it left the extraction's statements that the published text could not be read. Each of E1–E4 now says both 'in arXiv v2, the version read (the published version could not be consulted)' and 'Published version: …' in one locator. Their 'searched' lists still say 'the published text could not be read and it is not known whether these slips were corrected'. source.read still says 'The published version in the Annals of Mathematics could not be read here'. The register reproduces the contradiction, for example: '(the published version could not be consulted) Published version: the same two slips, at Proposition 5.1 on printed p. 322'. Separately, the note of item 10 is garbled: 'up to the factor q^{1+(g−1)r²} = q^{dim}/2 … more precisely q^{1−⟨α,α⟩}'. The factor is q^{(dim Higgs^st)/2}, not q^{dim}/2.
